notes: The use case is about the status of a Maintenance Duty, which due2 does not have. The closest ODRL is a remedial root obligation: the Provider must ex:refresh the dataset whenever it is older than PT6H. The age constraint reads a state operand, so it is a guard — it decides when the obligation is owed — and RL2's Active/Violated maps to not owed / owed and outstanding. Even so, no status can be compared here: an obligation is in force only for a request that some Permit or Forbid of its policy matches (§5.2), and this Agreement has none, so the obligation is never in force for any request and RL2's status is a monitoring answer, which due2 leaves open. The Offer and its Promise are dropped. The access decisions agree with RL2: no rule grants or forbids ex:inspect.

expected.why: The policy has no permission or prohibition, so nothing applies and ex:freshnessDuty is not in force (no rule of its policy matches). Its guard (PT2H > PT6H, F) would keep it out of force anyway, matching RL2's Active.

The guard holds (PT7H > PT6H), but no rule of the policy matches the request, so the obligation is not in force and is not reported; RL2's Violated status has no counterpart in the access question. Nothing applies.

scenarios.name: request for the obligation's own action

expected.why: An obligation is not matched by its own action (§5.2): with no Permit or Forbid in the policy, ex:freshnessDuty is not in force even for an ex:refresh request. No permission exists, so NotApplicable: an obligation to act is not a permission to act.
